column2: Frillish, Dragalge and Dhelmise make the submerged wreck distinct. Keep the deep-water preparation options and trace Dive access separately from first boarding the ship.
Mareanie and the coastal predators fit the flooded rooms; Lapras gives an attractive optional return. Room access and rod ownership, not nominal table levels, control first use.

Preserve the nine legacy selector tables as explicitly conditional data, with selector0 as the default. The expanded lower caves carry the active postgame diversity; do not count every selector as a normal simultaneous roster.
The broad postgame cave roster provides ready alternatives for exhibitions. Lucario, Spiritomb and Blissey have actual roles; high variety here is appropriate after a long campaign.
Keep Guzzlord as the exceptional deep-cave find and distinguish its Sign capture limit from repeatable ordinary species. Fishing adds routes that are not implied by the land roster.

Smeargle deserves stronger visual and dialogue identity, but preserve the useful broad collection. Its13% leading slot is a conscious broad-access choice rather than a broken probability. No automatic return to a monotypic cave.

The matching upper-floor roster is acceptable collection convenience in this small postgame location. Preserve Smeargle access and improve guidance through the world chapter instead of arbitrary species churn.

Fire-adapted wildlife and strong insects are convincing. Two redundant evolved birds yield space for Brute Bonnet and Bloodmoon Ursaluna; their original families retain much earlier acquisition paths.
Carbink, mineral Pokémon and the unusual Walking Wake slot reinforce an exceptional story site. Preserve its powerful choices and the ordinary/legendary source distinctions.

The mixed supporting roster is broad rather than tightly mineral. Retain it while the explicit Diancie landmark, stone and restored Wallace exhibition establish the chamber's identity; avoid moving many useful families for cosmetic purity.
The entrance provides cave residents before the deeper mineral/dragon discoveries. Keep the mix and treat story access as a separate requirement from species table levels.
Despite its legacy name, this is part of the expanded connected chamber sequence. Preserve mineral/dragon continuity and verify the actual warp route rather than excluding it by name.
The more evolved crystal/steel roster supports late team preparation. Preserve Archaludon and Goodra options and cross-reference reachable chamber progression.
Clefable, Metang and mineral residents suit the final approach to Diancie. Preserve the powerful late alternatives and the actual Diancie-room warp.

Ditto, burrowers and reconstructed fossils make a useful secret route. Add the three-segment Dudunsparce in a redundant Espathra slot, with Flittle retaining that evolution. Preserve this unusual collection and its connection from Sandstrewn Ruins; the fossil-maniac entrance gate alone does not define earliest access.
The abandoned captain's home gives early Ghost/Psychic choices without taking Duskull away from Mt.Pyre. Keep Mime Jr., Galarian Slowpoke and the broad haunted roster.

Keep butterflies, redirection/support candidates and Pheromosa. Early power is intentional ammunition, not a reason for automatic delay; test the actual nearby battles rather than infer imbalance from rarity labels.
Old Rod Mantyke40% is a direct low-cap success. Keep Magikarp60% beside it, the shore Rock Smash set and later Surf/fishing revisits as distinct acquisition methods.
Fire insects, furnace species and Blacephalon distinguish this hot optional passage. Preserve its exceptional encounter and the connection into Ashen Woods.
Keep the final coastal preparation pool and the five-species Super Rod set. The Waterfall approach and actual shoreline access must be represented in acquisition guidance.
Numel-country heat, Torkoal, gas and Fire types remain recognizable. Replace only a redundant Larvesta occurrence with Slither Wing, retaining its earlier forest acquisition.
Zubat, Geodude, Makuhita, Aron and Abra retain the original cave identity while Beldum and newer minerals expand choice. Preserve all12 entries and early high-ceiling options.
Sableye/Mawile, Bronzor, Meditite and mineral residents give a distinct deeper roster. Keep the alternatives and separate darkness/physical navigation from battle availability.

Duraludon, Deino and Tinkatink reward deeper exploration. Keep the ordinary table separate from Cobalion's landmark and Rock Smash access; neither is established by seeing a species in another method.
The steel/mineral roster makes Steven's chamber distinctive. Metang and Lucario are deliberate immediately strong options; retain them alongside their earlier forms.
Fighting, Ground, Fire and mountain dragons fit the slopes. Preserve the broad roster and bike/path distinctions; no proposal delays early Bagon merely to enforce a growth chapter.
Coastal Surf and rod pools provide useful late options near preparation services. Keep Lapras and Relicanth access and distinguish fishing choices from nearby route grass.
Numel, Slugma, stone and gas establish faction habitat immediately. Keep familiar residents and capable Fire/Ground choices during demanding story battles.
Noibat and evolved minerals vary the volcanic cave without losing Numel. Preserve the battle-ready reserve options rather than require raising only low forms.
The toxic pocket is distinguished by Koffing/Grimer and their support. Keep the Houndour/Salandit lines and the existing encounter levels under the global wild clamp.
The darker Fire roster complements the adjacent toxic chamber. Keep Houndour, Camerupt and Salazzle choices as practical alternatives to a single mandatory counter-team.
Evolved Fire threats are appropriate within the hideout's main confrontation. Preserve Darmanitan and Volcarona as optional player tools at the same time opponents use serious combinations.
The furnace-like chamber adds Chandelure and retains mixed offensive options. Same-family repetition supports convenient preparation rather than implying a required encounter rewrite.
This chamber retains unevolved Larvesta alongside developed Fire species. Keep the choice of immediate readiness or a preferred family; the Leveler removes level-grind pressure.
The climax floor gains Gouging Fire by replacing one redundant Magmar occurrence. Magby/Magmar remain available elsewhere; Camerupt and the volcanic identity stay intact.
Solrock/Lunatone, Bagon and rare mineral/dragon visitors make an excellent landmark roster. Preserve early Bagon elsewhere too; this site remains meaningful through density and its own discoveries.
Scream Tail replaces a repeated Clefairy occurrence while lunar anchors and Bagon stay. Rear-chamber physical access must not be conflated with first entry to the front cave.
Preserve the mature dragons and metallic plants. Distinguish its land roster, water methods, and legendary landmark; Waterfall/path prerequisites are documented by the world route.
Salamence, Dragonite and Roaring Moon make the remote chamber rewarding. Keep powerful ordinary discoveries and the Jirachi/Cresselia-related story paths separate.
The steel/stone collection gains Iron Boulder in a redundant Duraludon slot. Retain Metagross and Iron Crown, and keep Steven's authored team as a separate encounter obligation.
Sandshrew/Trapinch plus relic-like Ghost/Steel residents fit an archaeological entrance. Keep the meaningful fossil route and tower disappearance state distinct from catchable species.
Cofagrigus-line, golems and burrowing species support the ascent. Preserve the varied counter-building options and check bike/obstacle access through the existing puzzle.
Developed relic Pokémon make the upper floor feel deeper without withholding advanced strategy earlier. Keep its distinct Golurk/Claydol/Brongzong mix and stone interactions.
The evolved ruin roster suits the fossil summit. Preserve it and ensure the permanent Sandstrewn/Underpass route still supports later collection after the tower event.
Gimmighoul Chest provides a distinctive subterranean find among relics. Keep the basement gateway and its field encounters separate from the temporary above-ground tower.
Finizen and marine support Pokémon fit a research island. Keep the rod/Surf split and convenient access to late-team options near the Space Center sequence.
Shuppet and Duskull remain leading residents with familiar and modern Ghosts. Preserve the room as the clear entry into the Duskull family's dedicated habitat.
The second floor keeps Shuppet/Duskull and spirit flora. An Antique Sinistea variant can replace this floor's ordinary Sinistea while phony cups remain in earlier sources.
Lampent and the original ghosts provide increasing local variety. Preserve the roster and the actual indoor trainer paths rather than use cosmetic floor numbers as capture gates.
Mimikyu and Poltchageist broaden the tower's supernatural ecology. Keep all useful roles, including evolved ghosts available without a separate grinding requirement.
The upper floor keeps the original Ghost families and can distinguish artisan Poltchageist from counterfeit forms below. Preserve all unrelated roster entries.
Sinistcha, Houndstone and the mature original Ghosts support final preparations. Keep the Pecharunt/Giratina landmarks as separately gated interactions.
Vulpix, Meditite, Chimecho and unusual regional spirits preserve the familiar exterior identity. Keep Duskull here and distinguish exterior grass from internal ghost floors.
Flutter Mane is a powerful thematic discovery among spirits and mournful residents. Preserve it; the Darkrai NPC quest and relic story state require separate clear guidance.
Magnemite/Voltorb/Klink establish the station. Iron Thorns replaces a redundant evolved Eelektross slot while Tynamo and its evolution path remain available locally.

Keep technological families, Iron Hands and Wattrel. Rotom's scripted interaction, Meltan's landmark/evolution condition and ordinary encounters are distinct routes and must all be accurately explained.
The floating settlement offers ocean support and predator choices. Keep Finizen, Lapras and rod-specific differences; currents determine which other habitats are reachable from here.
Pond encounters and coastal-like fishing provide convenient return options after Surf. Preserve the method diversity and avoid claiming these water species are all available on the initial visit.
Preserve Shroomish/Slakoth/Wurmple with Caterpie, Ferroseed and the newly restored Burmy. This already meets broad early ammunition and woodland identity without another large reshuffle.
Cocoons, bugs, elemental monkeys and forest fruits make a distinct deeper section. Keep Paras and its useful support moves; Cut/path access is an actual requirement, not a badge-list guess.
Keep the diverse deep forest and early Kartana option. Its maze, optional water and Rock Smash methods make geography meaningful; dormant Hidden rows are not an extra native encounter method.
The opening has strong Hoenn anchors and baby/unevolved alternatives. Preserve its12-species roster around the new two-starter rescue and pre-rival catching loop.
Lotad/Seedot/Ralts/Surskit remain recognizable and Happiny/Togepi offer support choices. Preserve the roster so the first expert doubles battles have multiple available answers.

The Electric-rich roster is an intentional broad early resource after the user's clarification. Keep those options; improve the riverside identity through world context rather than an automatic availability nerf.
Mienfoo, babies, birds and plants give varied low-cap team-building. Preserve the eleven-percent Mienfoo and the fishing/Surf return layer independently of the initial woodland route.
The shoreline roster offers Water, Psychic and Fighting options. Verify actual grass/island access rather than assuming Briney's passage allows landing at every listed encounter tile.
Makuhita, Machop, coastal invertebrates and strong Fighting visitors suit Dewford's shore. Preserve Hawlucha/Falinks and the separate Rock Smash/capture methods.
The western shelf offers a distinct mix of fish and shallow-water species. Keep rod tiers and practical chances; boating past the route is not equivalent to Surf access.
Frillish, Dragalge and Dhelmise support the wreck-adjacent sea identity. Keep the shoreline fish pool and the Abandoned Ship connection as a worthwhile revisit.
The beach's Rock Smash pool includes Sandygast and Pincurchin, making a method-specific discovery worthwhile. Keep Surf and fishing availability separate from early beach trainer access.

Electrike, Gulpin, Plusle/Minun and urban newcomers establish the electrical corridor. Preserve the broad roster, including Pachirisu and Gimmighoul; resolve legendary clues without moving their gates.
Desert residents and Galarian Yamask fit the arid region. Retain Gible and other strong choices; the Dynamo rope, desert goggles and permanent cursed-stone path are separate physical requirements.
The plateau gains Sandy Shocks in a repeated Claydol slot. Preserve Rockruff's distinct form, Girafarig and other useful visitors, and use actual ruins access for guide text.
Keep the hot mountain approach's Fighting/Fire roster and Tyrogue. An optional early Tyrogue gift is a separate proposal only if it preserves this wild habitat; no need to remove the current entry.
Spinda, Skarmory and Spoink establish ash-route nostalgia. Preserve the new competitive choices around those anchors and avoid duplicate relocation merely for apparent rarity.
Swablu, Lombre/Nuzleaf and Zangoose/Seviper retain identity with varied visiting families. Keep the mixed roster and the separate river/rock methods that reward return exploration.
The northern grass roster supports useful families but is not on the same initial path as southern Seaspray access. Preserve the species and explicitly separate those physical areas in guidance.
Nincada, Skitty and the recent babies coexist with strong unevolved choices and Dreepy. Preserve all of them; low-level late bloomers are valid player choices rather than a pacing defect.
The Daycare meadow stays broad with Ditto and varied mammals/plants. The Old Rod gains Paldean Wooper while retaining Tympole, adding a missing functional line without another scarce hunt.
Linoone/Manectric preserve the familiar river corridor. Replace redundant Raticate/Porygon occurrences with Galarian Zigzagoon and Squawkabilly; their displaced families retain actual other routes.
Tropius, Goomy and rainforest residents stay with Raging Bolt. Hisuian Voltorb replaces a repeated final-evolution Kommo-o encounter; its base family remains earlier and elsewhere.
Keep Absol, Tropius and the mushroom/pumpkin ecology. The four Pumpkaboo sizes are deliberate form access; do not call them four entirely new species or remove mechanically distinct size options.

The city/haunted-country transition gains Alolan Grimer in a repeated evolved Hypno slot. Early Drowzee preserves Hypno access; Komala also yields space for a directly obtainable rare Maushold form while remaining on Route118.
The haunted island's surrounding water has Frillish and deep marine choices. Preserve the coastal context and avoid counting island access as reaching every Mt.Pyre interior immediately.
The Berry Master's countryside supports plants, insects, birds and orchard families. Preserve Karrablast/Shelmet access, their evolution methods and the separate garden-currency rewards.
The eastern sea offers Finizen, Mantine and useful rod catches. Retain the distinctive Dive layer rather than treating its surface and underwater species as one pool.
The cold approach to Shoal supports Spheal and marine options. Keep its rod-only Hisuian Qwilfish and the indoor tide-related discoveries distinct.
The Sootopolis perimeter has its own sea population and an underwater layer. Preserve the two as separate habitats with Dive requirements and appropriate story access.
The eastern approach provides Lapras, Mareanie and other marine tools near demanding trainers. Keep the accessible choices and the Keldeo-related landmark separate from fishing.
The cavern approach retains Wailmer, Sharpedo and strong marine combinations. Preserve Finizen and the distinct Seafloor/Dive entrances rather than flattening all acquisition into this route.
The southern ocean offers cold/deep visitors and special fishing forms. Keep the current roster while linking current-direction constraints to actual exploration.

Wynaut remains the leading Mirage Island resident. Preserve broad optional island diversity under the user's choice-first direction, while explicitly distinguishing rare island appearance from species slot chance.
Clamperl and Gyarados make a useful southern-water mix near Sky Pillar. Keep the Super Rod and Surf split and the story-controlled tower entrance separate.
Current-driven water exploration offers Wailmer/Finizen and different fish. Preserve usable catches and document one-way current access and return routes.
The currents include Spheal, Mantine and Lapras options. Preserve convenient collection rather than forcing repeated long current loops for an exclusive critical counter.
The Sealed Chamber approach keeps deep-sea residents and useful fishing forms. Its puzzle prerequisites belong to the landmark path, not every ordinary encounter in the surrounding water.

Whismur has the top slot and is uniquely associated with this tunnel; retain broad early alternatives including Chingling, Larvitar and Bagon. The prior suggestion to sacrifice this ammunition for a narrow roster is not adopted.

Imported regional forms, Kangaskhan, Tauros and Scyther make a strong collection destination. Preserve the roster and actual bike-area access; normal species collection remains distinct from the nursery Mega reward.
The extension's familiar Johto and evolved species remain useful postgame alternatives. Clearly record the extension opening rather than treating all Safari sections as immediately accessible.

The more developed Safari population complements the northern section and includes Ditto. Preserve Kangaskhan/Scyther access and all water-method distinctions; a redundant Ditto occurrence yields space for the Yellow Squawkabilly ability group.
The accessible imported-fauna section gains Galarian Meowth instead of repeated Porygon. Keep Alolan cats/Raichu, Chansey and the recognizable Safari collection mix.
The extension supports evolved Johto choices and special water methods. Preserve it as additional convenience without claiming the expansion gate is already open pre-League.
Swamp insects, Croagunk and Goomy families provide a coherent alternative Safari ecosystem. Keep their evolved catches and independent fishing choices.
Relic Ghost/Steel Pokémon and Great Tusk make an appropriate archaeological reward. Preserve unusual power and distinguish puzzle navigation from simple map registration.
Iron Treads distinguishes this excavated floor while repeated Claydol remains nearby. Preserve the remaining relic residents and all Rock Smash entries.
Evolved relics and Doublade fit the higher chamber. Keep the strategic variety; final access depends on the actual sequence of warps and obstacles.
Stakataka and Aegislash make the deep ruin distinctive. Preserve both powerful options with their different acquisition/capture-state rules.
The hot cave combines Fighting support, dragons and Fire types. Preserve the varied roster and separate water methods; the slab's expansion route is part of its identity.
Iron Moth replaces redundant Slugma to give the deeper hot chamber a missing exceptional species. Preserve Fire/Dragon residents and the separate Reshiram landmark.
The furnace roster and Heatran interaction fit the room. Keep physical-reveal and capture states distinct; the misleading name of a flag alone is not a defect.
Keep ordinary marine preparation at the entrance while Dive, the submarine and later cavern rooms remain distinct. Fishing rewards do not imply the story boulder route is open.
Marine predators and a cave resident make the room feel submerged. Preserve its varied offensive choices and its independent authored trainer encounter.
Sharpedo/Floatzel and deep-water bruisers distinguish this branch. Keep Basculegion and the cave bat rather than require one prescribed anti-Aqua team.
Dhelmise, relic Pokémon and defensive Water types fit the enclosed ruin. Preserve the palette and the nearby admin battle as separate content.
Keep Sharpedo, Malamar and the mixed marine offense. Its local cave geometry and partner-safe player options deserve preservation.
Tynamo and deep-water attackers distinguish the darker chamber. Retain the strong choices and the range of physical/special preparation roles.
The land roster and flooded section are separate encounter methods. Preserve both and document the current puzzle so players can actually reach the advertised water.
The defensive marine mix complements the adjacent water pool. Keep Toxapex, Golisopod and useful specialists rather than reduce the cave to repeated Zubat.
The final approach retains capable marine Pokémon plus Clobbopus/Dewpider options. Preserve the breadth immediately before Archie's demanding battle.
The early side cave supplies aquatic, Ground and unusual resistance options. Keep its current broad access; do not assume Rock Smash objects block every route to the lower floor.
Preserve the early Ice roster, babies and Frigibax. The user's choice-first direction supersedes a blanket plan to move these families later merely to reserve Shoal's novelty.
Spheal/Snorunt and familiar cave residents establish the cold habitat. Keep its water and fishing layer and explain tide access through actual map state.
Alolan Vulpix, Hisuian Sneasel, Iron Bundle and distinct forms give the room fresh value despite earlier Ice access. Preserve its meaningful discoveries and Mega rewards.
Galarian Darumaka replaces the repeated bat while original cold residents remain. Preserve water-method catches and the return route under tide changes.
Alolan Sandshrew replaces a repeated Seel occurrence, adding a missing Ice/Steel choice. Spheal/Snorunt and the remaining roster preserve the cave's signature.
The connecting cold roster supports convenient collection across the tide route. Keep Arctibax and core Ice families; a connecting room need not invent another exclusive species.
Ancient Ghosts, minerals and dragons support the tower's identity. Preserve the ready team options and the distinction between first story ascent and later exploration conditions.
Mature dragons and Metagross make the tower a valuable preparation destination. Preserve variety and verify actual bike/transition access before assigning an earliest capture cap.
The upper roster offers powerful final-team choices beneath Rayquaza. Keep those encounters separate from the scripted legendary's visibility/retry state.
The port's coastal methods complement its early NPC/gift interactions. Preserve the broad return roster and avoid treating its high authored water levels as early-game accessibility.
The crater lake retains its own Water roster and Finizen/Gyarados options. Story weather suppression and access to the town are separate conditions from catching after the crisis.
Preserve Dondozo and the deep, developed marine population. This is a real Dive reward rather than a reason to move useful surface species out of the game.
Clamperl's branches, Relicanth, Milotic and other deep residents make this underwater pocket distinct. Keep its variation and actual grass/terrain encounter access.
Dondozo/Tatsugiri remain the signature discovery. Add Droopy and Stretchy variants in redundant Kingdra/Wishiwashi slots while retaining each form at least5% and the submarine-only association.

Keep Cottonee, Deerling and the unusual Fairy/Psychic roster. Redundant evolved forms yield Galarian Ponyta and Iron Leaves; a separate hospitality gift supplies Indeedee-F without deleting the male form.
Preserve the mature final-team roster and first-floor Iron Valiant. Late acquisition should be immediately usable through the Leveler and preparation services.
Iron Jugulis replaces one repeated Noibat to distinguish the middle floor. Keep every other pseudo-legendary and advanced option rather than mandate raising a new team from scratch.
The deepest route retains final-team power and a separate water layer. Preserve its roster and the League handoff; repeated useful families are acceptable here.
